name: Track jobs or projects from start to finish
summary: Tracks each job or project from creation to close-out in the business's own system: ServiceM8 jobs and Asana projects. Crons read status and last activity, draft internal notes, and queue any client message for a person to approve. Nothing reaches a client without approval.

dispatched-field-jobs.evidence: 15 discovery calls describe this way of tracking jobs (field jobs dispatched to crews, most steps by hand)

covered_by.job-created: intake (ServiceM8 jobs in Quote or Work Order; Asana projects in the workspace)
covered_by.progress-updates: progress (stall check, draft note, queued client message)
covered_by.client-communication: progress and close-out queue client messages for approval
covered_by.record-keeping: intake and progress keep the tracking record

project-milestone-jobs.evidence: 15 discovery calls describe this way of tracking projects (milestones, costs and claims)

covered_by.progress-updates: progress (Asana task counts and last change)
covered_by.record-keeping: intake and progress keep the tracking record
covered_by.client-communication: progress and close-out queue project statuses for approval

unclear.evidence: 6 discovery calls describe a job system without a clear pattern

covered_by.record-keeping: intake and progress keep the tracking record

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Open ServiceM8 jobs and Asana projects, added to the tracking record once each.

crons.name: progress
crons.summary: Flag jobs with no change for the stall window (one draft note each), and queue a client progress message when there is new progress and the message window has passed.

crons.name: close-out
crons.summary: A finished job gets a draft close-out note and a queued completion message; an unsuccessful job is closed quietly.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, and an internal note on a ServiceM8 job or a task in an Asana project that only the team reads. A client message is a live operation: an email or SMS to the customer, or a project status that notifies every follower. Those are only queued, and run when a person approves them.

servicem8.covers: jobs in Quote and Work Order, status and last edit, internal job notes, client email and SMS about the job

asana.covers: projects in one workspace, task counts and last change, internal task notes, project status updates

gaps: Monday.com: mapped in the kit and named on many calls, but only two of its ten steps are fully supported, so no adapter this pass. Its ops are in the kit for a later adapter.
Simpro, Buildertrend, Vericon, Procore, Groundplan and Telegram job groups: named on calls, but their APIs are not mapped in the kit, so nothing reads or writes them here.
Scheduling and crew allocation: ServiceM8 allocations are mapped, but this build does not book crews or move jobs on a calendar.
Job setup (project plan, Gantt, job codes, cost centres): not built. Asana sections and Monday status columns would cover it once a person picks the structure.
Time and cost matching, materials ordering, variations and RFIs, and progress claims or invoices: not built. Owners keep these in Xero, spreadsheets or the job system by hand.
Stall detection uses the last change to the ServiceM8 job or the Asana tasks. A quiet job is a prompt to check it, not proof it is stuck.
Asana last activity is read from the first 100 tasks of a project, so a very large project can understate its last change.

Asana internal notes are tasks in the project, and a project status notifies every follower. Whether a client is a follower in the business's own workspace is not known, so Asana client messages are queued for a person to approve.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox account (ServiceM8 trial, Asana test workspace) proves it. Field names come from each vendor's official spec, checked in the endpoint map.

evidence.calls: 39 job-tracking calls read, 36 describe how they track jobs; every step runs 50 to 100 percent by hand
evidence.platforms: the vendors' own API operations for ServiceM8, Asana and Monday.com, mapped step by step; ServiceM8 and Asana have adapters, Monday.com does not yet
